transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-01-28
Start: 09:00 AM PT
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Priya Kapoor (CEO); Evan Li (CTO); Marta Gomez (VP Eng); Liam O'Connor (Head of Product); Sara Chen (Head of Sales); Diego Ramos (Head of CS); Nadia Brooks (Head of People); Alexei Volkov (Infra Lead); plus company-wide mute/rooms

Summary:
Priya opened with a short company update: strong usage growth in Hosted, traction on Dedicated deals, continued investment in Private for regulated customers. Evan reviewed runtime perf wins and upcoming infra work. Liam covered product roadmap reprioritization to accelerate Dedicated features and rollout policies. Nadia talked hiring cadence and org health. Short Q&A about hiring, SOC 2 timeline, and recent benchmark numbers. Meeting ended with clear next steps (benchmarks, roadmap doc, hiring Q&A).

Topics:
- Q4 usage & revenue signals
- Dedicated contract momentum and pilot wins
- Private (VPC/on-prem) sales and compliance asks
- Runtime performance wins (kernels, KV cache, quantization)
- Hiring plan and org health
- Roadmap adjustments for Q1

Transcript (timestamps approximate, transcription imperfect):
[00:00] Priya: hey everyone, thanks for joining on time, i know it's a heavy week so we'll keep to 45, 50 ish minutes, quick updates and then q&a, so first off big shout out team, product usage up over 2x qtr on qtr, hosted is driving adoption and we've got a few dedicated pilots moving into contracts
[00:28] Marta: yea, the infra team's been heads down, thanks to alexei and evan's folks we rolled a kernel change that drops p99 tail by ~15% for medium seq lengths, it's real but not magic y'know, still work to do on cold starts
[00:56] Evan: just to add, we saw the K V cache optimizations cut repeated prefix cost by about 22% in our internal benchmarks, some of that is the scheduling improvements, some is better kernel packing, the numbers vary a bit by model family though, so we'll share the spreadsheet after the call
[01:30] Liam: on product, we're shifting the roadmap a bit - Dedicated GA got bumped earlier, but there's more demand for fine-grained rollout controls and auto-fallback policies, customers want deterministic SLOs when a region or pool loses capacity
[01:58] Sara: quick sales note, several mid-market accounts are asking for Private (V P C) options and strict data residency, that's driving larger deal sizes but longer procurement cycles
[02:22] Diego: customer success is seeing the same trend; folks ask about SAML/SSO integration, audit logs, KMS support for keys, we closed a pilot by getting them a Private demo with HSM integration
[02:45] Priya: nice, on compliance - SOC 2 is on track, we got the Readiness report back, still a few config items to close, security team will post the timeline next week, can't promise dates but there's movement
[03:10] Nadia: hiring - we're hiring across infra and product, interviewing cadence picked up, reminder to everyone to submit referrals, we'll share headcount plan soon and there's a Q&A doc in the hr channel
[03:36] Alexei: infra notes, some of the kernel changes require new drivers in our Dedicated image, that's why some customers need a staged rollout; also a reminder - on-prem installers still have quirks with older OS variants, we are tracking the top 5 issues
[04:05] Evan: ok, i'll walk through a little deeper on the perf wins - we focused on continuous batching and a change to KV cache eviction that reduces repetition cost. in our 7B family internal bench we saw token cost drop and latency SLO improve at 95th but 99th still needs more work. i want to be clear: quantization profiles helped too, but model quality checks flagged a subtle regression in one eval for the 4-bit run so we rolled that back for the time being
[04:49] Marta: quick clarification, evan, when you say 4-bit regression, are we talking generation quality or logit bias?
[05:02] Evan: mostly slight generation drift on a specific prompt set, it's small but customer facing so we paused the rollout. we'll run more evals with improved calibration before enabling globally
[05:28] Priya: fine - we prefer slightly higher cost than shipping a bust to customers; reputation matters here
[05:40] [Laughter/unclear murmur] Speaker 7: uh-huh
[05:48] Liam: product roadmap note: we're prioritizing rollout and rollback primitives, better observability in Console per-route breakdowns, and a couple of QoS features for Dedicated (configurable autoscale policies). also working on more opinionated default batching heuristics to avoid one-size-fits-all that hurts latency for realtime workloads
[06:23] Sara: sales ask - can we get a short deck for Dedicated differentiators aimed at procurement? the deals team said procurement wants clear SLAs, fallback behavior, and an audit trail example
[06:45] Diego: i'll partner with sara on a customer-facing one pager, also i want to push a customer forum for pilot customers to share feedback and early wins, that will hopefully speed procurement by showcasing peers
[07:05] Priya: good. quick finance check - burn's in line with plan for Q1, committed bookings for Dedicated helped, still watching ARR conversion rates, marketing to push a few developer-focused benchmarks next week to push pipeline
[07:35] [pause, typing noise in background] Speaker 4: question about SOC two timeline from someone in the room, is there a target?
[07:44] Priya: security said mid-march is the target for readiness but external audit scheduling is variable, we'll firm it up next week, security will post a milestone doc
[08:05] Nadia: people update - new managers cohort starts next month, leadership training, please review the materials when they land; also mental health stipend change is live, HR posted details in the benefits channel
[08:29] [crosstalk] Speaker 2: can we talk about headcount prioritization for infra vs product?
[08:36] Priya: short answer - infra gets a little priority this quarter because of Dedicated ramp and some on-prem reqs, but we still keep product and DX hiring moving, we don't want feature starvation either
[08:52] Evan: on a more technical note, there were a few customer asks about VPC peering and split tunneling, i recommend our SEs have a doc that explains the network topology variations and the tradeoffs for latency vs security, we have a rough sketch in the confluence page but it's not formalized yet
[09:20] Marta: also raising an FYI - some internal tests flagged a memory leak in a GPAllocate path on older CUDA drivers, we've got a patch but it needs validation, we'll put it into the next canary image
[09:46] Liam: roadmap specifics - timeline changes: Dedicated GA still Q2 but some features like per-route SLAs and automatic fallback are now Q1 targets for the teams that need them to close deals. Private deliveries will be staged: VPC first, on-prem second, full offline air-gapped later in the year
[10:16] Sara: sales pipeline highlight - three deals in legal for Dedicated, one strategic partner wants a longer term reserved capacity commitment, that looks promising but legal terms are longer than usual, procurement asked for sample contract language
[10:40] Priya: legal to post a sample and sales to push a checklist for procurement items - sara, diego, coordinate on that
[10:49] Diego: will do
[10:54] [11:00-ish mark noise] Speaker 9: question about customer-facing benchmarks, when will those be public?
[11:04] Evan: we plan to publish a developer benchmark set next week; it's lightweight but shows latency/cost tradeoffs for small models and medium sequences; we'll avoid naming customers and will indicate hardware specs. again caveat: internal numbers, they vary with prompt distribution
[11:25] Nadia: reminder to managers - performance review calibration next month, please fill the sheets on time
[11:34] Priya: closing notes - thanks for everyone's hustle, small ask: share a win in #company-wins channel this week, helps morale. we'll follow up with the roadmap doc and the perf spreadsheet. quick recap of next steps: evan shares benchmarks, liam posts roadmap, nadia collects hiring Qs, diego/sara prepare procurement one-pager and customer forum.
[12:00] Q&A (quickfire)
[12:10] Employee 1: question about remote-first policy and more in-person meetups?
[12:18] Nadia: we're keeping remote-first but will schedule two regional meetups this spring, budget and details to come
[12:28] Employee 2: can the se team get a short network topology doc?
[12:33] Evan: yes - will publish a network topology and V P C peering doc by next week, will include tradeoffs for latency and security
[12:45] Employee 3: are we still targeting SOC 2 next quarter?
[12:52] Priya: mid-march target for internal readiness, external audit TBD
[13:05] [wrap-up] Priya: thanks all, meeting adjourned, check the channels for the docs, and please flag blockers in your 1:1s.
